subject: How accurate cutting supports a better fit
hook: Will panels cut to my list actually fit? That depends as much on the list as on the saw.
fb:
A question we hear from trade customers most weeks: if I send you a cutting list, how do I know it will fit?

The honest answer is that a square, accurate cut is only as good as the list behind it. A few habits make all the difference:
• Give finished sizes, length then width, every time
• Mark which edges get ABS edging (0.4, 1 or 2 mm)
• Show grain direction on oak-effect and woodgrain boards
• Name the board, colour and thickness

We look over lists before they go to the saw and query anything that does not add up. Ask us for a priced cutting list here:
https://superiofurniture.com/panel-cutting/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=autumn-interiors-and-practical-comfort&utm_content=day-049
gbp:
How do I make sure cut panels fit my job?

It is the most common question from trade customers sending work to our Hanley workshop. Panels are cut on a sliding table panel saw and checked for squareness, but the fit on site depends just as much on the cutting list.

For the best result:
- List finished sizes, length first, then width
- Mark which edges need ABS edging, in 0.4, 1 or 2 mm
- Show grain direction on oak-effect and woodgrain boards
- State the board type, colour and thickness

We look over every list before cutting and query anything that does not add up, such as a door wider than its opening or a shelf deeper than its carcass. We can also drill hinge cups and shelf-pin rows and assemble cabinets, so panels arrive ready for the next stage.

Joiners, fitters and cabinet makers across Stoke-on-Trent and Staffordshire are welcome to send a list for a priced breakdown. Trade and domestic orders welcome.
